quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean the same way you lean.
Sit as far back on the seat as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean the same way the driver leans. They should sit as far forward as comfortable and hold firmly onto the driver's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best formation to stay close while keeping safe distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while leaving safe space between them. Use a single-file line when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: When using a sidecar to carry a load, you should:

options.text: Allow the load to move freely.
Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not shift and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place loads toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the sidecar nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: A major effect of alcohol is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down both your physical and mental abilities.

questions.question: During your pre-ride check, what should you NOT inspect?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam light, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your following distance.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of cars ahead to see farther. Use your high beam, except when you are following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Any time you are slowing or stopping
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads
Only when slowing or stopping in an emergency
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you are slowing or stopping
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: To make a quick stop on wet pavement, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when making a quick stop on a slippery surface. The front brake is safe to use on slippery pavement if you apply it gradually to prevent locking.

questions.question: A proper lane position helps you do all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster.
questions.explanation: Your lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid other drivers' blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: The driver will not necessarily yield to you.
The driver will definitely yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver will not necessarily yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver will yield just because you made eye contact. Drivers often look at motorcyclists but still do not see them.

questions.question: Which of these protects your face the best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility on the road?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothing, keep your headlight on all the time, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Which of these should NOT be part of your pre-ride inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your paint.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. Perform this inspection every time before you ride.

questions.question: How is passing different for motorcycles than for cars?

options.text: A motorcycle must be seen more easily than a car.
A motorcycle does not need to be seen as much as a car.
Pass on the shoulder instead of the road.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle must be seen more easily than a car.
questions.explanation: The basic passing rules are the same for motorcycles and cars. However, visibility is more important for motorcycles. Motorcycles are smaller and can easily disappear into blind spots or be missed by other drivers.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycle brakes is true?

options.text: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
The rear brake is stronger than the front brake.
Both brakes have the same stopping power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Should you follow another vehicle more closely at night or during the day?

options.text: Follow at a longer distance at night.
Follow at a shorter distance at night.
Use the same distance at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow at a longer distance at night.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances in the dark because you cannot see shadows or light contrasts. Use a longer following distance at night than you do during the day.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: What kind of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you ride?

options.text: Stay on the right side of your lane.
Stay on the left side of your lane.
Use your rearview mirrors more than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from the cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out from between cars. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: When a driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: It does not mean they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver will yield just because they make eye contact with you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still do not notice them.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent. Use your arms to steer, not to hold up your body. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you balance during turns.

questions.question: Approved helmets:

options.text: Can limit how far you can see.
Let you see as far to the sides as you need.
Do not have to be worn if you think they limit your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let you see as far to the sides as you need.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets do not dangerously limit your vision. They allow you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Riders should generally:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions often to avoid boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. Choose the lane position that gives you the most space around you and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, they should pass:
questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. The next rider should wait until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before beginning to pass. Continue this pattern until all riders have safely passed.
